Reconcile current board/officer titles and signatory authorities against executed minutes, resolutions, SEC GIS, and bank mandates.
Correct all live profiles and templates that state an 8% option or show future-only officers as current.
hard_stops: no filing without source workpapers and human approval
no payment instruction from public/client documents
no deletion or overwrite of source evidence
no declaration of full compliance without current certificates and filing proofs

15_design_research_engine.purpose: Govern how body-region content is structured and styled: always research the best presentation for the specific content, always re-express it through the locked GSSC token vocabulary, always check against real persistent precedent before deciding, never invent outside the token system, never operate from memory isolation.
15_design_research_engine.human_note: Applies only to the EDITABLE BODY region defined in 10_template_engine / Execution Protocol Section 22. Masthead, margins, footer, watermark, marginalia and the canonical signature lockup remain governed by 03_brand and 10_template_engine and are NEVER touched by this module.

scope.governs: how new or existing body content (text blocks, cards, tables, and any novel visual element such as a chart) is structured and styled for a specific deliverable, every single generation
does_not_govern: locked chrome (masthead, margins, footer, watermark, marginalia, signature lockup)
canonical identity, governance, firewall, IP (those remain 01/02/04/05 authority)
commercial/legal/research content itself (Execution Protocol Sections 05-21 still govern what facts may appear)

trigger.rule: Every body-content decision is freshly re-examined on every generation. There is no complexity threshold and no exemption for content that has an existing anatomy (cards, tables). A valid outcome of re-examination is 'the existing pattern is still correct, keep it' -- freshness means the decision is genuinely re-made, not that the output must differ from before.
trigger.cost_disclosure: This trigger policy is deliberately more expensive than a threshold-gated design (research/reasoning runs on every body element, every document). Accepted by GSSC management 2026-08-05 in exchange for consistently thought-through, client-facing design quality.

delegation_topology.fleet_context: When operating inside the GSSC EXPIRA fleet, the RESEARCH stage below routes to the Research specialist agent as a genuine subagent delegation, per the existing intent-routing pattern in 12_bootstrap.
delegation_topology.single_model_context: When operating as a licensed/derivative deployment with only one model available (no fleet, no delegation), the SAME five-stage loop runs, performed serially by that single model inside one reasoning pass. The doctrine is identical in both cases; only the execution topology differs.

stage_1_research.action: Investigate the best way to present this specific content (chart-vs-table-vs-prose selection, arrangement, emphasis), drawing on real editorial/design precedent for the content's actual shape (trend, comparison, single figure, narrative). This explicitly includes spatial alignment, relative sizing, and balance between simultaneously-visible elements (for example: should two grid cells align to the same baseline, does one figure need to be visually larger to reflect its importance, should a label's font size change to fit its allotted width). Where 10_template_engine.layout_budget_reference.collision_and_balance_reference has flagged an imbalance or fit risk for existing content, treat that objective finding as an input to this research decision, not a replacement for it -- decide the best content-level or arrangement-level fix, then re-check with Stage 4.
stage_1_research.evidentiary_discipline: Same anti-fabrication standard as Execution Protocol Section 05: cite the precedent or pattern basis relied on. Never assert a design choice is 'best practice' without a real, statable basis. This applies equally to spatial/balance decisions: cite the design basis for a chosen alignment or relative sizing, do not assert it is simply 'better' without a statable reason.

stage_2_translate.action: Re-express whatever Stage 1 recommends using ONLY the existing GSSC token vocabulary already declared in 03_brand.visual_system and the quotation/document doctrine CSS custom properties (color palette, type scale, rule-weight grammar, spacing rhythm, opacity values).
stage_2_translate.hard_gate: This stage never relaxes. A structurally novel layout is permitted; a novel COLOR, FONT SIZE, SPACING VALUE or BORDER WEIGHT outside the existing token set is not. If no existing token fits, stop and flag for a versioned kernel/brand update -- do not invent an ad hoc value silently.

stage_3_integrate.action: Place the translated result inside the editable body region only, respecting the content-fit hierarchy already defined in Execution Protocol Section 23.

stage_4_selfcheck.action: Verify: no clipping/overflow, no overlap, every color/size/spacing value traces to a declared token, locked chrome untouched, geometry unchanged. For TEXT BLOCKS, apply the computable estimation method in 10_template_engine.layout_budget_reference (character-count-based height estimate against fixed page/column geometry, 0.85 safety margin). For MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUSLY-VISIBLE ELEMENTS (grid cells, side-by-side content), apply layout_budget_reference.collision_and_balance_reference: the AABB overlap test to confirm no unintended collision, the grid-row balance check (30% threshold) to catch visual imbalance even when there is zero literal overlap, and the fixed-width horizontal fit check for any non-shrinking element with allotted width (e.g. a flex-shrink:0 label).
stage_4_selfcheck.known_limit: These estimations (text-block height, 2D collision, row balance, horizontal fit) are calibrated approximations confirmed working via both real prior-session content (a genuine 33.3% grid imbalance was caught retroactively in this session's own earlier output) and constructed test cases (forced overlap, forced imbalance, forced horizontal overflow all correctly detected). None of this is a rendered-pixel check -- no headless browser or HTML/CSS rendering engine and no working package installer exist in this environment as of 2026-08-06 (checked directly). It reduces, but does not eliminate, the value of an eventual literal rendered confirmation if such a tool becomes available.
stage_4_selfcheck.executable_now: The collision, row-balance and horizontal-fit checks this stage has always instructed the model to "apply" became executable at 2.16.0: gridbalance. Until then the instruction could only be followed by hand, which is why the 33.3% imbalance in the doctrine text is a one-off anecdote rather than a regression test.

stage_5_selffix.action: On any Stage 4 failure, apply Execution Protocol Section 23's escalation order (tighten/consolidate/prioritize/flag) before ever reconsidering geometry. If the failure stems from the Stage 1 choice itself being unworkable, cycle back to Stage 1 with a simpler ask rather than forcing a bad fit.

technical_constraints.novel_visual_elements: Any new visual primitive (chart, comparison graphic, etc.) must be constructed in pure HTML/CSS or inline SVG only. No external JavaScript charting library, no CDN dependency. Preserves the existing single-file, offline, no-external-dependency portability principle already followed by the authorized quotation/document masters.

memory_mandate.rule: Never decide in isolation and never treat a generation as a blank/first-ever instance. Before Stage 1, read relevant prior entries from the Design Decision Log. After Stage 5 passes, write a new entry. This is mandatory, not optional, on every generation. Beyond simple reference-or-divergence, treat prior entries as continuous-improvement input: each generation should explicitly consider what, if anything, can be refined relative to the closest relevant precedent, and state that refinement -- or the deliberate, reasoned choice not to refine -- in the logged rationale. The objective is that each iteration is at least as good as, and where a genuine improvement is identified, better than, the last.

store.detection_policy: STORAGE-AGNOSTIC. Detect and use whatever persistent, queryable memory store the current deployment actually has, in this priority order: (1) a Dataverse table, using the canonical field set below mapped to that deployment's own Dataverse column names; (2) a SharePoint or equivalent list, using the same canonical field names as list columns; (3) a flat structured file (JSON/CSV) in OneDrive, Drive, or any other accessible file store, using the same canonical field names as keys/columns; (4) any other persistent, queryable memory system already available to the host model or agent (a vector store, database, CRM record, or similar), mapping the same canonical fields onto whatever native schema that system exposes. Only if NONE of the above exist may the engine fall back to session-local memory, and it MUST then explicitly disclose in its output that no persistent store was available and precedent continuity does not survive beyond the current session.
store.gssc_reference_mapping: GSSC's own production deployment maps these canonical fields to Dataverse table cr746_designdecisionlog with columns cr746_document_reference, cr746_client_name, cr746_content_type, cr746_body_structure_used, cr746_is_novel_pattern, cr746_design_rationale, cr746_tokens_referenced, cr746_date_generated, cr746_source_versions_used, cr746_precedent_reference. This is GSSC's concrete instance of the detection policy above, not the only permitted store: a licensed or derivative deployment is not required to use this exact table, prefix, or even Dataverse itself -- it must use SOME persistent store from the priority order above, mapped to the same canonical field names, so the doctrine remains portable across whatever memory system the host environment actually provides.
store.gssc_current_deployment_instance: Where Dataverse is not reachable, the package runtime implements detection_policy tier 3 directly: a flat JSON sidecar named by design_decision_log.store_filename, created beside the package on first write. It is deliberately a SIDECAR and never the package itself, because a control package is versioned and immutable while a decision log grows on every generation. Read with: python gssc_runtime.py precedent <package>.

memory_mandate.metadata_discipline: Every field is populated by logic drawn from the actual current task -- the real client name, the real content type, the real tokens actually used, the real kernel/protocol/template versions in effect. Never a fabricated or placeholder value. If a field is genuinely unknown, mark it explicitly rather than guessing.
memory_mandate.read_before_decide: Query prior entries for the same client and/or same content type before Stage 1, to inform (not dictate) whether this generation should deliberately match, deliberately diverge from, or deliberately improve upon precedent.
memory_mandate.write_after_decide: Log the decision actually made, citing which (if any) precedent entry it referenced, intentionally departed from, or improved upon, via the precedent_reference field, and stating the specific refinement identified (or the reasoned absence of one).
memory_mandate.build_integration: LIVE as of 2.16.0, verified by execution. The 2.15.0 kernel stated that "the release build itself writes a Design Decision Log entry through log_decision(), closing a gap recorded at 2.14.0 ... Precedent continuity now begins from this release." It did not. Verified 2026-09-22 by three independent means: (1) every call site of log_decision( across the whole 1.7 runtime was the `def` line itself -- dead code; (2) the `logwrite` verb documented in the runtime header was never added to argparse choices and exited with "invalid choice"; (3) `precedent` reported 0 entries against a package that has produced dozens of real client documents. The mandate said "write after every decision" while nothing wrote, for four releases. 1.8 wires the write to the ONE genuine generation event -- `hydrate -o`, an emitted file -- and adds the missing logwrite verb. Proven by control: a read-only audit leaves the entry count unchanged; a build raises it by exactly one. Section 46 now fails the build if the write path ever loses its caller again.
memory_mandate.write_trigger_rule: The log records BUILDS, not audits. hydrate() is a pure read called by clipcheck, footercheck, boxcheck and gridbalance to obtain the document; logging there would write an entry every time anybody ran a check and turn precedent into noise. The hook lives only on the path that emits a file.

failure_modes: Inventing a color/size/spacing value not in the existing token set
Touching locked chrome to accommodate a body design decision
Deciding in isolation without reading the Design Decision Log
Fabricating a design-precedent citation
Using an external JS charting library or CDN dependency for a novel visual
Logging fabricated or placeholder metadata to the Design Decision Log

16_continuous_optimization_discipline.purpose: Govern how genuine lessons learned through user interaction become permanent, versioned kernel/protocol doctrine, while strictly preventing subjective preference from being mislabeled as an objective improvement, fix, or optimization.
16_continuous_optimization_discipline.human_note: This module governs changes to the KERNEL AND PROTOCOL THEMSELVES (the governing doctrine), distinct from 15_design_research_engine, which governs per-document body-content decisions. Think of 15 as document-level memory/iteration and 16 as doctrine-level memory/iteration.

scope.governs: whether and how a suggestion, correction, or discovery arising from a user interaction is captured as new or amended kernel/protocol doctrine
scope.does_not_govern: per-document body design decisions (15_design_research_engine) or canonical identity/governance/firewall/IP facts (01/02/04/05, changed only from verified source information per 00_meta.override_tiers)

materiality_gate.rule: Before any change is logged or framed as an optimization, fix, or improvement, it must pass ALL of the following. A change failing any test may still be implemented if the user requests it, but MUST be logged as a preference honored, never as a fix or optimization.
tests: OBJECTIVE_BASIS: the change removes or reduces a measurable inefficiency (redundant bytes, redundant computation, an unimplemented doctrine gap, a demonstrated defect or failure) rather than merely reflecting taste or style.
NO_UNREQUESTED_CONTENT_CHANGE: the change does not alter any information, content, or functional output the user did not ask to change.

INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIABLE: the claimed improvement is checked by an objective method (hash comparison, byte-count comparison, structural/schema validation, a passing test) and that check is reported, not merely asserted.
materiality_gate.failure_mode: Calling a subjective or preference-driven change an 'optimization' or 'improvement' when it has no measurable, verifiable basis is a hallucination of value and is prohibited. State plainly when a change is preference-only.

capture_and_versioning.rule: A change that passes the materiality gate becomes permanent doctrine: implement it, version the affected kernel module(s) and/or Execution Protocol section(s) following the existing versioning and changelog discipline (00_meta / 13_changelog and the Protocol's own Section 32 change record), and never silently reintroduce a previously-fixed inefficiency in a later version. If a later version appears to reintroduce a pattern a prior changelog entry fixed, flag the regression explicitly rather than proceeding silently.
capture_and_versioning.session_continuity: A genuine lesson learned in one session must not be lost at the end of that session. Capture it into the kernel/protocol itself (this is the mechanism) rather than relying on informal memory of the conversation, so a future session starting fresh from the current kernel/protocol automatically inherits the lesson without needing to rediscover it.

self_assessment_discipline.rule: When asked for a self-assessment, score, or completeness estimate of the kernel, protocol, or any generated deliverable, ground every component of the score in a concrete, checkable criterion (a specific verified fact, a named remaining gap, a measured byte/percentage figure) rather than an unexplained number. State remaining gaps honestly, including gaps this module itself cannot close (for example, a genuine need for a rendered-pixel verification tool that does not currently exist in the operating environment).

priority_relative_to_generalization.rule: While preparing this kernel/package for use as a licensable, generalized derivative, changes that also concretely benefit GSSC's own current, real use (smaller/faster/more reliable files, clearer doctrine, fewer defects) are preferred over abstractions that only matter for a hypothetical future derivative and provide no benefit to GSSC today. Generalization work should not degrade GSSC's own present deliverable quality, correctness, or efficiency.

failure_modes: Labeling a subjective preference change as a fix or optimization in a changelog entry
Implementing a change that silently alters content or output the user did not request
Claiming a byte/behavior improvement without independently checking it
Losing a genuine lesson learned at the end of a session instead of capturing it into kernel/protocol doctrine
Silently reintroducing a previously-fixed inefficiency in a later version without flagging the regression
Giving a self-assessment score with no stated, checkable basis for each component

claim_evidence_rule.rule: No kernel doctrine field may assert that a behaviour is implemented, validated, or closes a gap unless the same release adds or updates an executable check that would FAIL if the claim were false, and that check is DEMONSTRATED to discriminate -- shown failing against a negative-control fixture, not only passing against the real document.
claim_evidence_rule.why: Every defect found in the 2.15.0 audit was this one rule being absent. collision_and_balance_reference claimed three dated validations for code that did not exist. memory_mandate claimed a live write hook for a function with no caller. The runtime header claimed `all` ran geometryaudit and a logwrite verb existed; neither was true. In each case the prose was plausible, internally consistent, and wrong, and nothing could tell.
claim_evidence_rule.discrimination_requirement: Passing is not evidence. A check that has only ever returned PASS is indistinguishable from a check that cannot return anything else. The first Section 44 AABB draft passed the real document perfectly and was structurally incapable of ever failing.
claim_evidence_rule.false_positive_requirement: The control runs in BOTH directions. A check that fires on a correct document is overridden, then ignored, then removed. The second Section 44 draft reported six real-looking collisions that were all false.
claim_evidence_rule.executable: gssc_runtime.py wiringaudit <package.json>  +  the release negative-control suite

upstream_deletion_rule.rule: A completeness guarantee is only valid over the inputs it can actually see. Any stage that DROPS, FILTERS or SKIPS content upstream of a coverage check must declare what it drops, and that declaration must itself be audited. Otherwise the coverage check reports full coverage of a reduced input and reads as proof when it is not.
upstream_deletion_rule.origin: The 2.16.0 page-4 footer overlap. The coverage ledger correctly reported 0 unaccounted elements on a page where 190px of chart was invisible, because the parser had already deleted it. Both statements were true simultaneously.
upstream_deletion_rule.generalisation: Ask of every audit: what did this never get to look at? That is where the next defect of this class lives.

17_numbering_and_toc_system.purpose: Govern how structural units are numbered, how their headers are set, and when and how a table of contents is generated. Numbering style and header aesthetic are a function of a declared category, not one flat convention.
17_numbering_and_toc_system.human_note: Read with 03_brand. This module owns the ordinal and the header register; 03_brand still owns the type scale, palette and rhythm those registers draw from.

scope.governs: ordinals, category words, header registers, contents-page generation and its trigger
does_not_govern: the type scale, palette, tracking and rhythm themselves (03_brand)
locked chrome: masthead, margins, footer, watermark, marginalia, signature lockup
what facts may appear in a section (Execution Protocol Sections 05-21)

17_numbering_and_toc_system.indexable_rule: A category declares whether its headers belong in a contents list. Navigational and subordinate headers -- toc_entry_ref, figure_chart, legal_section, sub_item_minor -- declare indexable false. Found during the 2.10.0 build's own first repass: the contents page carries a CHS header in the toc register, and an extractor that treated every CHS header as a section indexed the contents page inside its own contents list and shifted every subsequent ordinal by one.
17_numbering_and_toc_system.roman_ceiling_rule: A roman ordinal past XXXIX is unreadable in a running header. Past a category's declared ceiling the dispatcher falls back to the declared fallback_style. The fallback is deterministic and declared, never a silent truncation.

categorical_header_system.purpose: One header skeleton, five quiet registers keyed to category and archetype. Replaces the legacy .section > .marker header.

design_basis.doctrine_drift_closed: Kernel 2.9.0 recorded 03_brand.document_type_system.inherited_literals_px.section_numeral = 26.0px, but the quotation master shipped .section .marker .num at 56px, .page.p2 at 48px and .page.p3 at 46px. The refined numeral was written into doctrine and never applied to the template. CHS closes that drift rather than inventing a new number, and lands below the declared literal at 13px.
design_basis.hierarchy_inversion_corrected: The legacy header set the ordinal at 56px against a --fs-section 9px title: a 6.22:1 ratio in which the least semantic element on the page outweighed the name of the section it numbered. Editorial practice is the reverse -- an eyebrow label supports the heading it introduces and conventionally sits at roughly 40-60% of it, grouped tightly above. CHS primary sets the ordinal at 0.68:1 of the title.
design_basis.register_not_ornament: Editorial work favours consistency over novelty across a sequence of pages; a header treatment that delights once becomes tiring by the tenth. CHS therefore ships one skeleton and five registers rather than five headers.
design_basis.measure_reclaimed: The legacy marker reserved a 76px grid column for the ordinal. The CHS stamp is an eyebrow above the title, so the title now sets on the full 540px body measure.

primary.note: Default editorial register. Title dominates; ordinal recedes to a gold jewel.

legal.note: Flatter, statutory register. Sans uppercase title reads as instrument, not article.

formal.note: Zero-latitude archetypes are undecorated: no descriptor, strongest rule.

plate.note: No rule: the figure frame already supplies the edge. Two rules would fight.

minor.note: Lowest register. Stamp and title share one line; no rule, no descriptor.

toc.note: Contents opens in the primary proportion so it reads as a peer of the sections it indexes.

legacy_inversion.note: Recorded so the audit can state the before/after ratio from data rather than from memory.

hard_gates: Every size, colour, tracking and rhythm value must resolve to a token already declared in 03_brand or in this module's token_px table.
No register may set the ordinal larger than the title it numbers.
The CHS layer ships as its own <style id="gssc-chs-extension"> so it can be audited in isolation.
Legacy .marker CSS is preserved, never deleted: an unconverted header must still render as before.
categorical_header_system.page_overrides_note: A class-keyed resolver cannot see a font-size rule scoped by page. The Section 38 cover overture styles .page.p-cover .body h1.title with --fs-dropcap, so the title renders at 64px while a class-only lookup still costs .title at 42px. That is the same defect class as the chs-title substring overcharge arriving from the other direction, and the cover overture introduced it. Caught by Section 37 parityaudit on its first run against the build that created it. Every page-scoped override is declared here and resolved by the runtime, never inferred.

v2_changes.toc_leader: The contents row was a 3-track grid holding 4 children, so auto-placement created an implicit fourth column sized to the leader's own intrinsic content -- empty, height:0. The leader could never stretch and the dot leader could not render as specified. Grid has no primitive for "let one item consume the space between two others"; flex-grow does. The row is now a flex row and the leader is its only growing child.
v2_changes.toc_hierarchy: The contents ordinal and title both sat at --fs-dek 13px, separated only by colour -- 1.00:1, contradicting the subordination principle CHS enforces everywhere else. The ordinal drops to --fs-caption 10px: 0.77:1. Stated reason: a reader looks a section up by TITLE and uses the ordinal only to confirm, so the title leads there for the same reason it leads in a header.
v2_changes.eyebrow_contrast: The category eyebrow shipped mid_grey at 3.70:1 against ivory at 8px, below the small-text floor. Moved to slate, 6.96:1, which remains visibly recessive against the navy title.

categorical_header_system.token_note: --fs-title was registered in 2.12.0 when the cover revert returned the cover title to it. Sections 33A and 37 both failed on the first repass of that build until it was registered, which is the intended behaviour: a token in use and absent from the registry is a defect, not a detail.

v3_changes.category_chip: The category word becomes a bordered chip with its own ground, so it is a visual object rather than letter-spaced text. The registers were hierarchically correct but the entire visual event of a header was one 34px gold terminal.
v3_changes.bracket: A short navy rule above the stamp mirrors the terminal below, so a header reads as bracketed rather than only closed.
v3_changes.category_accent: The tick carries the category colour -- gold for primary, teal for legal, clay for plate. Hue is never the only signal: the ordinal and the category word both still say it in text.

categorical_header_system.toc_depth: Contents rows gain a category-keyed left tab and weighted ordinals. The ordinal keeps its SUBORDINATE SIZE -- the inversion corrected in 2.11.0 is not reintroduced -- and gains weight and a colour tab instead, so the contents page previews the document's category logic at the one place a reader sees the whole structure at once.

toc.build_order_rule: Pagination settles FIRST, the contents page is generated SECOND from the settled folios. Generating a contents page before the page count is final produces folios that are wrong the moment an annex expands the document -- the gap recorded in the 2.10.0 draft, now a binding rule.
toc.ordinal_rule: Contents ordinals are re-derived through the category dispatcher, never copied from whatever numeral happens to be hardcoded in the body, so the contents page self-corrects when a section is inserted or removed.
toc.leader_rule: The dot leader reuses the master's own margin-rail dotted language and is implemented as the single flex-growing child of the contents row. It must never be placed as a grid item: an implicit auto-sized column collapses it to zero width, which is exactly how 2.10.0 shipped a leader that could not lead.

failure_modes: Scanning for a bare class="num" and picking up the commercial-table right-alignment utility of the same name as if it were a section ordinal.
Setting an ordinal larger than the title it numbers.
Introducing a header font size, colour or tracking value outside the declared tokens.
Generating the contents page before pagination settles.
Copying body ordinals into the contents page instead of re-deriving them.
Deleting the legacy .marker rules rather than superseding them.

18_page_archetype_creativity_engine.purpose: Tell the generating model, region by region rather than page by page, how much creative latitude a given piece of a document carries and which existing module owns the rules for it.
18_page_archetype_creativity_engine.human_note: This is a routing and lookup layer. It creates no new authority over locked chrome; 03_brand, 06_quotation_doctrine and 09_legal_doctrine remain the substantive owners and are cross-referenced per archetype.
18_page_archetype_creativity_engine.why_region_not_page: Verified by direct inspection of the universal master: page p3 (folio 05 after 2.10.0 repagination) carries the Section III Commercial Terms body -- fully researchable under Module 15 -- and the canonical signoff block with the signature lockup, which carries zero latitude, on the same physical page. A page-level creative posture is therefore structurally wrong for this master.

budget_scale.0: Verbatim. Module 15 Stage 1 research is skipped entirely. Any deviation is a hard stop of the same tier as 04_firewall and 05_ip.
budget_scale.1: Token-constrained micro-variation only. Stage 1 runs but is narrowly scoped to already-approved states.
budget_scale.2: Full Module 15 five-stage loop, bound by the normal token vocabulary.
budget_scale.3: Full Module 15 loop plus a mandatory external precedent check before Stage 2, because this is where a model is most likely to reach for an untokenized value or generic stock imagery.

cover.note: The only budget-3 archetype. Live precedent check is mandatory.

budget_3_pass.status: ATTEMPTED 2026-09-21, MEASURED, AND REVERTED the same day. The treatment raised the cover title from --fs-title 42px to --fs-dropcap 64px at max-width:470px. Measured by the Section 23D resolved box model: the 68-character title wraps to six lines, 430.1px, driving page 1 to 1059.4px against an 843px budget -- a 216px overflow into the footer band. Reverted to 42px on the full column: three lines, 141.1px, page total 770.4px, 72.6px spare.
precedent_basis: Scale dissonance between display and body type is the dominant recurring device in contemporary editorial practice, and the cover is specifically the page that must earn attention before anything else does.

The isolation effect (von Restorff, 1933) holds only while the isolated element remains the exception: if everything is emphasised, nothing is. The correct move is therefore to raise exactly ONE element and leave every neighbour untouched.
budget_3_pass.execution: Cover title --fs-title 42px -> --fs-dropcap 64px. Both tokens were already declared in the master :root; no new literal was introduced. Open space above the title widened so the raise reads as composition rather than a larger font. Kicker let down to a hairline-ruled eyebrow so the title is the single entry point. Nothing else on the page changed.
budget_3_pass.measured_effect: Display-to-body dissonance returns to 4.00:1. The 6.10:1 figure claimed at 2.11.0 was real but unaffordable.
budget_3_pass.photography: None introduced. 03_brand.photography.default is "avoid when possible" and the treatment is compositional and typographic only.
budget_3_pass.content_integrity: No content added, removed or reworded. The change is entirely a restyle, so Module 16 NO_UNREQUESTED_CONTENT_CHANGE is satisfied.
budget_3_pass.finding: The cover of this master cannot carry a scale-dissonance overture at its current content load. Measured headroom for the title box is 213.7px; 44px fits with 17px spare, 48px already overflows by 1px, and neither margin is safe. An overture needs SPACE, not only size, and space on this page would have to come from content -- which Section 38 forbids a cover overture from touching. The correct conclusion is that the page must be shortened editorially before any overture is attempted, which is a content decision for management, not a design decision for this module.
budget_3_pass.retained: The kicker eyebrow refinement is kept: hairline rule beneath the kicker, gold-deep, with declared rhythm spacing. It costs 8.5px, measured, and it was never the cause.

table_of_contents.fill_note: The contents page of the universal master measured 30.7% fill against a 91.5% cover: a 60.8-point spread, the widest in the document. Luxury-editorial practice treats generous white space as confidence, but a spread that wide is not composition, it is an unfilled page. Adding the metric strip and roadmap -- both genuinely navigational content, which is what a contents page is for -- moved it to 48.9% and narrowed the document spread to 42.6 points. Measured, not asserted.

locked_elements: firewall: no itemized cost, supplier attribution or margin wording
registered_patterns: tier_comparison (03_brand.component_registry) -- budget 1; a registered anatomy, not a fresh composition

chart_data_visualisation.note: Pure HTML/CSS/inline-SVG only; no external library or CDN.
chart_data_visualisation.first_exercised: Performed 2026-09-21. The archetype was fully specified and had never been built against: grep for <svg> on the 2.12.0 master returned zero, so series-to-palette mapping was a declared variable with nothing to select from. A horizontal bar figure now ships on the commercial page, built from pure inline SVG with no library and no CDN, drawing on the new data_series_palette.
chart_data_visualisation.redundant_encoding_rule: Colour never carries meaning alone. Every series declares a pattern as a second channel and prints its value as a text label, so the chart survives monochrome print and the red-green deficiency carried by roughly 8% of men.

signatory_acceptance.note: Zero latitude. Renders in the CHS formal register: no descriptor, strongest rule.

notarial_acknowledgment.note: Zero latitude. CHS legal or formal register only.

18_page_archetype_creativity_engine.composite_page_rule: Where a page carries more than one archetype, each region is resolved independently and the LOWEST budget in play governs any decision that spans them. A budget-0 region never inherits latitude from a budget-2 neighbour.
failure_modes: Assigning one creative posture to a whole page that carries mixed archetypes.
Treating a budget-0 region as merely conservative rather than verbatim.
Reading this module as authority to relax a rule owned by 03, 04, 05, 06 or 09.
Running a budget-3 archetype without the external precedent check.
Using an external charting library or CDN for a chart archetype.

budget_gate.rule: NO archetype treatment at any creativity budget may push a page past its content budget. The page budget is a hard constraint that outranks every creative latitude in this module, including budget 3.
budget_gate.enforcement: Section 23D boxcheck must PASS on the built derivative before any archetype treatment is adopted. A treatment that fails is reverted, not rationalised.
budget_gate.origin: Added after the 2.11.0 cover overture shipped a 216px footer overflow. The treatment was reasoned from genuine precedent and was still wrong, because no gate connected the creative decision to the page it had to live on.
budget_gate.capacity_rule: Before adding ANY block to a page, read that page's current fill from Section 23D. A page reporting AT CAPACITY (>= soft_fill_limit_pct) has no room: place the block elsewhere or relocate existing content first. The 2.16.0 commercial page was at a true 95.8% when a tier block was added to it, which is how it reached 110.2% and crossed the footer. The measurement existed; it was not consulted before the edit.

19_accessibility_doctrine.purpose: Govern the accessibility of GSSC client-facing documents, and state honestly and in one place what is currently guaranteed and what is not.
19_accessibility_doctrine.human_note: This module exists because nothing else did. Modules 01-18 govern type, colour, geometry, overflow, governance and collision, and none of them said anything about whether a document can be read by a screen reader.

current_state.source_floor: ENFORCED. A declared document language, a non-empty title, a text alternative on every image, and a label or explicit aria-hidden on every figure. Checked on every run by Section 45 and demonstrated to fail on fixtures missing lang and missing alt.
current_state.pdf_structure: NOT GUARANTEED, AND DISCLOSED. The approved print workflow (Chrome/Edge, Ctrl+P, A4, margins none, background graphics on, 100%, Save as PDF) emits an UNTAGGED PDF by construction: no structure tree, no tagged table headers, no explicit reading order. Every GSSC PDF released to date is in this state.
current_state.why_not_closed: No tool capable of writing PDF structure exists in the operating environment -- re-confirmed 2026-09-22 alongside the rendering-engine check: no Chromium, no Playwright, no WeasyPrint, no wkhtmltopdf, no Prince, no pagedjs-cli, and no working package installer. LibreOffice is present and is already disqualified as a conversion path by Module 10. Claiming conformance without a tool that can produce it would be the exact failure class 2.16.0 was written to end.

19_accessibility_doctrine.commercial_relevance: PDF/UA or WCAG 2.1 AA conformance appears as boilerplate in an increasing share of institutional and enterprise procurement requirements. GSSC pursues exactly that class of client. A document can be visually immaculate and still fail an accessibility review outright, and none of the existing design QA can see it.
19_accessibility_doctrine.required_action: When a tagging-capable tool becomes available -- Chrome DevTools Protocol tagged-PDF export, Acrobat Pro, or a Python tagging library -- extend this module to a full PDF/UA gate and supersede this text. Until then the source floor is the guarantee and the gap is stated, never implied closed.
failure_modes: Asserting PDF/UA conformance that no tool in the pipeline can produce
Dropping lang, title, or alt in a future template edit
Treating a passing Section 45 run as evidence of PDF accessibility
Adding an unlabelled inline SVG figure

GSSC QUOTATION RESEARCH AND EXECUTION PROTOCOL
Version 2.1 | 25 August 2026
Owner: GSSC Integrated Corporation
Classification: INTERNAL CONTROL DOCUMENT
Status: AUTHORITATIVE CONTROL CANDIDATE — READY FOR MANAGEMENT ADOPTION

======================================================================

======================================================================
FILE_ROLE: RESEARCH_AND_EXECUTION_PROTOCOL
PROTOCOL_VERSION: 2.0

DESIGN_RESEARCH_ENGINE_REQUIRED: YES

DESIGN_DECISION_LOG_STORE: Dataverse table cr746_designdecisionlog OR equivalent SharePoint/Drive list
CHANNEL_FAILURE_FALLBACK_REQUIRED: YES
INLINE_VERIFICATION_RENDER_ALLOWED: YES -- SEE SECTION 28B, NARROW EXCEPTION TO THE SECTION 28A NO-BINARY-IN-CHAT RULE
CONTINUOUS_OPTIMIZATION_DISCIPLINE_REQUIRED: YES -- SEE SECTION 22B AND KERNEL MODULE 16
LAYOUT_BUDGET_CALCULATOR_AVAILABLE: YES -- SEE SECTION 23A AND KERNEL MODULE 10.layout_budget_reference (TEXT-BLOCK ESTIMATION ONLY, NOT A RENDERED-PIXEL CHECK)
COLLISION_AND_BALANCE_CHECK_AVAILABLE: YES -- SEE SECTION 23B AND KERNEL MODULE 10.layout_budget_reference.collision_and_balance_reference (2D ESTIMATION, NOT A RENDERED-PIXEL CHECK)

======================================================================
01. PURPOSE AND OPERATING PRINCIPLE
======================================================================
This protocol controls the complete path from a client request to a researched,
commercially defensible, client-safe GSSC quotation produced from the exact
attached GSSC template source.

The controlling principle is:

RESEARCH BROADLY. VERIFY CURRENTLY. PRICE INTELLIGENTLY. PROTECT GSSC.
DISCLOSE SELECTIVELY. PRESERVE THE TEMPLATE EXACTLY. NEVER INVENT.

This protocol has two linked engines:

ENGINE A — Research, costing, risk, legal and commercial positioning.
ENGINE B — Client-safe extraction and exact source-preserving conversion.

Research determines approved content. The attached authoritative template
determines the document. Research never authorizes redesign.

The permanent input layers are separate and must not be blended:

1. DOCTRINE LAYER — the current attached GSSC production kernel.
2. ASSET LAYER — the current attached authorized Base64 logo or asset payload.
3. STRUCTURE LAYER — the current attached authoritative quotation template.
4. EXECUTION LAYER — this protocol.
5. PROJECT LAYER — the current client request, research, specifications,
   drawings, quotations and supporting evidence.

The internal research dossier and the client quotation are separate outputs.
Internal economics, supplier information, legal analysis and negotiation limits
must never leak into the client-safe quotation.

======================================================================
02. AUTHORITY, PRECEDENCE AND CONFLICT HANDLING
======================================================================
Use the following order when sources conflict:

1. Current government-issued certificates, laws, regulations and official
   regulatory guidance verified for the current task.
2. Current executed or authoritative corporate records.
3. Current locked GSSC master files and the attached authoritative template.
4. Current GSSC production kernel.
5. The client's current written request and confirmed technical requirements.
6. Current verified market, supplier and labor evidence.
7. Clearly labeled reasoned assumptions.
8. Older profiles, drafts, summaries, prior quotations and chat recollections.

Do not silently choose a convenient value. Record the conflict, identify the
sources, apply the highest verified authority, and flag any conflict that could
materially change scope, price, legality, risk or delivery.

A filename containing FINAL does not by itself prove that a document is current,
executed, approved, notarized or authoritative. Inspect content and status.

Do not allow an older template, profile, quotation or draft to override current
GSSC identity, governance, tax status, public contacts or firewall rules.

CONTROL RELATIONSHIP:

- The kernel controls canonical identity, governance, firewall, IP, doctrine,
  registry and source-priority rules.
- This protocol controls the project research sequence, commercial analysis,
  management gate, client-safe extraction and conversion workflow.
- The decoded template controls exact layout, DOM, CSS, assets, geometry and
  print behavior for the named template role.
- The project record controls confirmed current scope and management-approved
  commercial decisions.
- No layer may silently override a higher-priority control or perform a function
  assigned to another layer.

======================================================================
03. STARTUP COMMAND AND REQUIRED FILE INSPECTION
======================================================================
Before researching, drafting or modifying any file:

1. Load and apply the attached GSSC production kernel.
2. Inspect every attachment before acting.
3. Read brand_assets and inventory the exact assets. Each asset is stored once,
   single-encoded, with its own decoded-image SHA-256. Verify every asset decodes
   and that its hash matches the declared value.
4. Decode the quotation payload and inspect its actual HTML, DOM, CSS, scripts,
   assets, page geometry, typography, page breaks and print rules. The stored
   payload is the TOKENIZED template: binary assets appear as {{GSSC_ASSET:name}}
   placeholders. Hydrate per Section 28C before rendering or delivering anything.
5. Identify the current client request and all project-specific supporting files.
6. Classify every input.
7. Confirm whether the task is research only, preliminary pricing, final
   conversion, revision, audit or client release.
8. Use the least-destructive source-preserving operation.

Do not begin the final quotation merely because a template and client name are
present. Complete the research, commercial, approval and firewall gates first.

If an essential source cannot be read or decoded, stop final conversion, state
the exact missing or unreadable input, and do not fabricate a replacement.

PACKAGE PREFLIGHT — REQUIRED PASS/FAIL REPORT:

RUN IT, DO NOT READ IT. The package carries an executable implementation of this
preflight in the runtime part. Extract and run it:

    python gssc_runtime.py preflight GSSC_Master_Package.json

It exits 0 on PASS and 1 on PRECHECK FAILED, and prints one line per check. The
prose below remains the governing specification; the runtime is its executable
form. If the two ever disagree, the prose governs and the runtime is the defect.
Manual execution of these checks remains acceptable where Python is unavailable.

- Confirm the master package is present, readable and valid JSON, and that all
  six top-level parts are present: manifest, kernel, execution_protocol,
  quotation_template_payload_base64, brand_assets and assembly.
- Validate the kernel object and report its internal kernel version.
- Confirm the kernel has exactly the module count declared in
  manifest.integrity.kernel_module_count, and exactly one changelog entry
  marked current.
- Validate quotation_template_payload_base64 as strict Base64 before decoding.
- Confirm the decoded TOKENIZED template begins with <!DOCTYPE html> and ends
  with </html>. Do NOT apply this markup test to brand_assets: those are binary
  image payloads and must instead decode to their declared MIME type with a
  matching sha256_of_decoded_image.
- Confirm every {{GSSC_ASSET:name}} token in the template resolves to an entry in
  brand_assets, and that no brand_assets entry is orphaned.
- Record the SHA-256 fingerprints declared in manifest.integrity in the project
  record, and recompute them using manifest.integrity.hash_method.
- Confirm the quotation source role: finished source-derived master, category
  master, geometry baseline, or universal template. Do not assume universality.
- If the template contains prior project content, treat it as source content to
  be replaced only in authorized variable regions; never carry prior client,
  pricing, date, specification or project facts into the new quotation.
- If any preflight check fails, label the package PRECHECK FAILED and do not
  proceed to client release.

======================================================================
04. INPUT CLASSIFICATION AND PROJECT INTAKE
======================================================================
Classify each attachment as one of the following:

- governing kernel
- authoritative quotation master or template payload
- authorized logo or asset payload
- client request
- drawing, measurement or site image
- bill of quantities or technical specification
- supplier quotation
- market reference
- labor-rate reference
- legal or regulatory source
- earlier quotation
- internal calculation
- executed agreement, purchase order, NTP or SOW
- working draft
- unknown source requiring inspection

Create a PROJECT INTAKE record containing:

- formal client legal name
- client short name
- attention person and verified title
- project or program title
- location and worksite
- request date and quotation deadline
- requested delivery, installation or completion date
- exact scope requested
- quantities and units
- dimensions and measurements
- required brands, grades, materials, finishes or performance criteria
- inclusions
- exclusions
- client-provided items
- site conditions
- procurement requirements
- required permits, licenses, testing or documentation
- payment or billing requirements stated by the client
- warranty requirements
- requested alternatives or options
- open questions
- assumptions requiring approval

Unsupported information must be marked PENDING CONFIRMATION. Never invent a
quantity, measurement, specification, lead time, legal requirement, warranty,
commercial term, price or client fact to complete the document.

======================================================================
05. RESEARCH STANDARD AND SOURCE DISCIPLINE
======================================================================
Research must be current, project-specific, geographically relevant and based on
comparable scope. Use official and primary sources first where available.
Cross-check material commercial conclusions using multiple independent sources
when practical.

For every factual or monetary research item, record:

- fact or amount
- currency
- tax basis: VAT-inclusive, VAT-exclusive, Non-VAT or unknown
- source title
- source publisher or provider
- source date or observation date
- geographic basis
- technical and scope basis
- whether delivery is included
- whether installation is included
- whether warranty is included
- retail, wholesale, distributor, contractor or turnkey classification
- verification status
- confidence: HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW
- limitations or comparability adjustments

Never combine values with different tax bases without first normalizing and
showing the arithmetic internally. Never present an unknown tax basis as known.
Do not fabricate citations, prices, quotations, statutes, wage orders, permits or
technical standards.

Research is evidence, not authority to overwrite a management-approved amount.
Once management selects the commercial position, do not silently change it.

======================================================================
06. MARKET-RATE RESEARCH
======================================================================
For each product, service, work package or complete program, investigate:

- local market rate
- Western Visayas or relevant regional rate
- Philippine national benchmark where useful
- low-market reference
- median or ordinary-market reference
- upper-market reference
- premium or turnkey reference
- material-only price
- supply-and-delivery price
- supply-and-install price
- fully managed turnkey price
- date and validity of each reference
- technical comparability
- brand, grade, capacity, dimensions and performance
- VAT or Non-VAT basis
- freight, installation, mobilization, testing and warranty coverage
- procurement channel and minimum order
- lead time and availability

Do not compare unlike scopes as if they were equal. A low online material-only
listing is not a direct comparable to a GSSC turnkey engagement containing
sourcing, validation, controlled delivery, installation coordination,
documentation, warranty administration and single-point accountability.

Required market conclusion:

- LOW MARKET REFERENCE
- MID-MARKET REFERENCE
- UPPER-MARKET REFERENCE
- PREMIUM/TURNKEY REFERENCE
- SCOPE AND TAX NORMALIZATION
- COMPARABILITY ADJUSTMENTS
- CONFIDENCE LEVEL
- RECOMMENDED GSSC MARKET POSITION

======================================================================
07. SUPPLIER AND ACQUISITION RESEARCH — INTERNAL ONLY
======================================================================
Evaluate, where applicable:

- quoted total and line coverage
- VAT-inclusive, VAT-exclusive, Non-VAT or unknown basis
- quotation validity
- stock and availability
- delivery and freight
- handling and unloading
- installation or commissioning support
- lead time
- minimum order
- payment requirements
- warranty and replacement responsibility
- returns and defects handling
- technical compliance
- capacity and reliability
- price-change exposure
- foreign exchange exposure
- missing line items
- exclusions
- likely variation exposure
- execution and dependency risk

Supplier names, contacts, addresses, quotations, prices, bank information,
representatives, sourcing routes, comparison-bid arrangements and shadow-bid
arrangements are INTERNAL ONLY and must never appear in client content.

Do not characterize a supplier quotation as GSSC's actual cost basis unless the
current internal commercial record expressly confirms that treatment.

======================================================================
08. MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT AND CONSUMABLES RESEARCH
======================================================================
For physical work, identify and quantify where supported:

- principal materials
- dimensions and measured quantities
- grades, thicknesses and finishes
- fittings, fixings and accessories
- coatings and finishing materials
- consumables
- cutting and fabrication loss
- normal wastage
- packaging and protection
- replacement allowance
- testing materials
- freight and handling
- storage
- tools and equipment
- lifting or access equipment
- temporary works
- disposal and clean-up requirements

Separate the internal analysis into:

DIRECT MATERIALS
ACCESSORIES AND FIXINGS
CONSUMABLES
WASTAGE
PACKAGING
FREIGHT
HANDLING
EQUIPMENT
TESTING
DISPOSAL
CONTINGENCY

Do not expose internal item-level cost, supplier attribution or margin mechanics
in the client-facing quotation. Use bundled client-safe scope descriptions and
approved bundled prices.

======================================================================
09. LABOR, PRODUCTIVITY AND FULLY BURDENED COST RESEARCH
======================================================================
Labor research is mandatory whenever execution requires human work.

Verify for the relevant location and task:

- current applicable statutory wage floor
- prevailing skilled-trade market rate
- helper or general-labor market rate
- foreman or supervisor rate
- professional service rate where applicable
- crew composition
- estimated productive hours and workdays
- overtime, night, weekend or holiday exposure
- transportation
- meals and accommodation where applicable
- statutory or contractual labor burden where applicable
- PPE and safety requirements
- safety officer, permit or induction requirements
- equipment operator requirements
- mobilization and demobilization
- installation difficulty
- occupied-premises inefficiency
- restricted work windows
- access and lifting constraints
- testing and commissioning labor
- snagging and rework allowance
- warranty call-back allowance

Distinguish internally:

1. statutory minimum baseline
2. actual competitive skilled-market rate
3. fully burdened internal labor cost
4. market-facing labor value

Do not price skilled or supervised work automatically at minimum wage. Do not
invent labor productivity. State assumptions and use conservative allowances
where current evidence is incomplete.

======================================================================
10. LOGISTICS, MOBILIZATION AND SITE-COST RESEARCH
======================================================================
Assess:

- origin and destination
- route and verified distance where relevant
- vehicle type and trip count
- fuel
- tolls, parking, ferry and access fees
- loading and unloading
- lifting and rigging
- building permits, gate passes and inductions
- delivery-hour restrictions
- staging and storage
- security
- traffic or access constraints
- disposal
- clean-up
- return visits
- failed-delivery risk
- remobilization risk
- inter-island or special handling
- weather exposure

Include logistics and site constraints in the fully loaded internal cost and risk
analysis. Do not assume free delivery, unrestricted access or a single successful
visit unless confirmed.

======================================================================
11. TECHNICAL, SAFETY AND REGULATORY RESEARCH
======================================================================
Determine whether the scope requires:

- manufacturer instructions or certifications
- Philippine National Standards or other applicable standards
- building, electrical, structural, plumbing, mechanical, sanitary,
  environmental, food, water, fire or occupational-safety compliance
- local permits or clearances
- licensed professionals or accredited contractors
- approved drawings or calculations
- product certifications
- inspection
- testing and commissioning
- maintenance instructions
- warranties
- operating manuals
- turnover documentation
- as-built records
- safety plans, PPE or method statements

Distinguish GSSC's coordination and business-support role from regulated work.
Do not state or imply that GSSC or its personnel directly perform regulated work
for which a required professional license, permit or accreditation has not been
verified. Where lawful performance requires a qualified or licensed party,
state that requirement internally and use client-safe wording consistent with
the contract and verified delivery arrangement.

Flag uncertain compliance questions for qualified Philippine counsel or the
appropriate licensed professional. Do not invent legal or engineering conclusions.

======================================================================
12. LEGAL RIGHTS, OBLIGATIONS AND CONTRACTUAL PROTECTION RESEARCH
======================================================================
The objective is not to find one-sided arguments. Identify the applicable legal
and contractual framework, GSSC's legitimate rights, GSSC's obligations, the
client's obligations, material risks and issues requiring professional review.

Research and evaluate, as applicable:

A. CONTRACT FORMATION AND AUTHORITY
- authority of the client signatory or representative
- quotation acceptance mechanics
- relationship to the CMSA, SOW, PO or NTP
- mobilization or procurement authorization
- validity period
- order of precedence
- change control and variation orders

B. PAYMENT PROTECTION
- downpayment or mobilization funding where justified
- milestone billing
- invoice trigger
- due date
- late-payment treatment
- suspension rights
- approved variation reimbursement
- cancellation costs
- storage and remobilization
- client-caused delay
- retention of title where applicable and legally appropriate

C. SCOPE AND CLIENT DEPENDENCIES
- accuracy of client-supplied information

TRIGGER -- ALWAYS ON:

FIVE-STAGE LOOP:

1. RESEARCH -- investigate the best way to present this specific content

3. INTEGRATE -- place the translated result inside the editable body region

4. SELF-CHECK -- verify no clipping/overflow, no overlap, every color/size/

Do not depend on an external JavaScript charting library or a CDN resource.
This preserves the single-file, offline, no-external-dependency portability

MEMORY MANDATE -- ALWAYS MEMORY-BASED, NEVER ISOLATED, ITERATIVELY IMPROVING:

Never decide in isolation and never treat a generation as a blank first-ever

22B. CONTINUOUS OPTIMIZATION AND ANTI-HALLUCINATION DISCIPLINE (GOVERNED BY KERNEL MODULE 16)
======================================================================
Apply this section whenever a user interaction surfaces a possible correction,
efficiency gain, or doctrine gap in the kernel or this protocol itself -- as
distinct from Section 22A, which governs per-document body-content decisions.

MATERIALITY GATE -- REQUIRED BEFORE LABELING ANYTHING AN OPTIMIZATION OR FIX:

A suggested or discovered change may be logged and framed as an optimization,
fix, or improvement only if it passes ALL of the following:

1. OBJECTIVE BASIS -- it removes or reduces a measurable inefficiency (redundant
   bytes, redundant computation, an unimplemented doctrine gap, a demonstrated
   defect or failure), not merely taste or style.
2. NO UNREQUESTED CONTENT CHANGE -- it does not alter any information, content,
   or functional output the user did not ask to change.
3. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIABLE -- the claimed improvement is checked by an
   objective method (hash comparison, byte-count comparison, structural or
   schema validation, a passing test) and that check is reported, not merely
   asserted.

A change that fails any of these tests may still be implemented if the user
requests it, but MUST be logged as a preference honored, never as a fix or
optimization. Calling a subjective or preference-driven change an
"optimization" when it has no measurable, verifiable basis is a hallucination
of value and is prohibited.

CAPTURE AND VERSIONING:

A change that passes the materiality gate becomes permanent doctrine: version
the affected kernel module(s) and/or this Protocol's relevant section(s)
following the existing changelog discipline (Kernel 00_meta/13_changelog and
this Protocol's Section 32 change record), and never silently reintroduce a
previously-fixed inefficiency in a later version. If a later version appears
to reintroduce a pattern a prior changelog entry fixed, flag the regression
explicitly rather than proceeding silently.

A genuine lesson learned in one session must not be lost at the end of that
session -- capture it into the kernel/protocol itself so a future session
starting fresh automatically inherits it without needing to rediscover it.

23A. LAYOUT BUDGET CALCULATOR -- COMPUTABLE OVERFLOW ESTIMATION (GOVERNED BY KERNEL MODULE 10 / 15)
======================================================================
HONESTY NOTE: this is a calibrated approximation, not a verified per-glyph
font-metrics engine and not a rendered screenshot. No headless browser or
HTML/CSS rendering engine (Chromium, Playwright, WeasyPrint, wkhtmltopdf) and
no working package installer (pip/npm) were found available in the operating
environment as of 6 August 2026 -- confirmed by direct search, not assumed.
This method reduces, but does not eliminate, the need for a literal rendered
check; if such a tool becomes available in a future environment, supersede
this method with literal rendered measurement per Module 16 non-regression
discipline.

GEOMETRY CONSTANTS (extracted directly from the quotation master's own CSS,
not assumed): page height 1123px; margin-top 96px; margin-bottom 120px; body
column width 540px (fixed, non-responsive); body padding by page -- Page 1
38/26px, Page 2 32/22px, Page 3 30/26px (top/bottom).

FONT SIZE AND LINE-HEIGHT REFERENCE (px): fs-body 10.5, fs-bodyL 11.5,
fs-title 42, fs-dek 13, fs-kicker 8, fs-caption 10, fs-section 9.
Line-height ratios: lh-body 1.58, lh-display 1.12, lh-lede 1.65, lh-tight 1.4.

ESTIMATION FORMULA:

1. Average character width = 0.50 x font-size-px. This is a commonly used
   design heuristic for proportional Latin body text, NOT independently
   verified against the actual Inter/Libre Baskerville font metrics tables
   (no internet-fetched font-metrics data available in this environment).
2. Characters per line = column-width-px / average-character-width-px.
3. Estimated lines = character-count / characters-per-line, rounded up.
4. Estimated block height = estimated-lines x (font-size-px x line-height
   ratio).
5. Available budget = (page-height - margin-top - margin-bottom) - page's
   body padding-top - body padding-bottom - height already used by prior
   elements on that page.
6. Safety margin = 0.85. Treat the block as fitting only if estimated block
   height is at or below 85% of the available budget, absorbing kerning,
   ligature, and hyphenation variance the flat character-width approximation
   does not capture. Above that threshold, treat it as AT-RISK and apply the
   Section 23 escalation hierarchy before finalizing.

VALIDATION ON RECORD (6 August 2026): calibrated and sanity-checked against
the master's own existing, presumed-working text blocks -- Page 1 lede
paragraph (301 characters, computed at 12.8% of remaining budget), Page 1 dek
paragraph (530 characters, 20.2%), Page 2 sig-desc block (286 characters,
5.8%) -- and against constructed forced-overflow scenarios, including a case
with 2,340 characters against only 100px of remaining budget, which correctly
computed as AT-RISK at 381.6% fill. Both the PASS and AT-RISK verdict
branches were confirmed to compute correctly from real arithmetic, not an
always-true default.

SCOPE LIMIT:

This method estimates TEXT BLOCK height only. It does not estimate or verify
image clipping, decorative-element overlap, CSS rendering defects, font-
loading failures, or any other non-text visual issue. Those remain governed
only by the qualitative construction-rule review already defined for Stage 4
self-check; treat this calculator as a genuine reduction in correction
iterations for text overflow specifically, not a complete substitute for
eventual visual/rendered confirmation.

======================================================================
23B. COLLISION AND BALANCE DETECTION (GOVERNED BY KERNEL MODULE 10 / 15)
======================================================================
Extends Section 23A's single-block vertical estimate to genuine 2D layout
risk: unintended overlap between simultaneously-visible elements (grid cells,
side-by-side content), visual imbalance between elements meant to read as
parallel or equal-weight, and horizontal overflow risk for fixed-width,
non-shrinking elements. Still not a rendered screenshot -- models element
geometry as axis-aligned bounding boxes from the template's own fixed CSS
constants (column counts, gaps, fixed widths).

AABB OVERLAP TEST:

Two boxes (x, y, width, height) overlap if and only if:
ax < bx+bw AND ax+aw > bx AND ay < by+bh AND ay+ah > by.
Verified 6 August 2026 against a deliberately overlapping pair (correctly
returned true) and a correctly-spaced 2-column pair (correctly returned
false) -- both branches confirmed, not a default.

GRID-ROW BALANCE CHECK:

For cells sharing a grid row, row height equals the maximum of that row's
cell heights (matching real CSS Grid auto-sizing behavior). Imbalance percent
= 100 x (max cell height - min cell height) / min cell height. Flag as
VISUALLY UNBALANCED above a 30% threshold -- an editorial-design heuristic
for when a reader would notice unequal weight between elements presented as
parallel choices, not an exact rendered measurement.

Validated 6 August 2026 against the REAL Page 2 research-grid content from
this session's own prior dynamic-body-design test output: correctly
identified a genuine 33.3% height imbalance between two grid cells that had
not been previously noticed without this check -- a concrete finding on real
content, not only a synthetic demonstration. Also confirmed against a
deliberately extreme forced case (699.4% imbalance), verifying the threshold
fires correctly at the extreme end too.

FIXED-WIDTH HORIZONTAL FIT CHECK:

For an element with a fixed width and a non-shrinking constraint (for
example flex-shrink:0), estimate whether given text fits on one line within
that width: characters per line = allotted width px / (0.50 x font-size px);
lines needed = ceiling(character count / characters per line). If the
surrounding CSS does not permit wrapping and more than one line is needed,
this is an overflow risk requiring attention before finalizing. Tested 6
August 2026 against the template's actual Page 3 bar-chart label constants
(150px width, 8px font-size): a 33-character label correctly estimated to
fit on one line; a 62-character label correctly estimated to require 2 lines.

USAGE:

These checks feed Stage 4 self-check as objective data. They inform, not
replace, the Stage 1 research decision on how to adjust a flagged layout --
see Section 22A's research stage, which explicitly includes spatial
alignment, relative sizing, and balance between simultaneously-visible
elements within its scope. Decide the best content-level or arrangement-level
fix using research judgment, then re-check with this section's calculations.

SCOPE LIMIT:

the patterns present in the current template. A genuinely novel future

formula added at that time, per Section 22B's continuous-optimization

28A. DELIVERY, FILE-SIZE AND DOWNLOAD ENGINEERING
======================================================================
A completed deliverable is not delivered until the recipient can actually open
it. Apply the following delivery discipline.

FILE-SIZE DISCIPLINE:
- Keep the self-contained HTML as small as brand and print quality allow.
- Embed each large Base64 asset ONCE. Where a masthead logo, seal, signature
  lockup or watermark repeats on every page, reference a single embedded copy
  through CSS (for example, content:url(...) on the element) instead of pasting
  the same payload into every page. In Chrome and Edge this renders byte-for-byte
  identical to a repeated src while dramatically reducing file size.
- This single-embed deduplication is lossless and preserves the print system. It
  is not a redesign and does not alter geometry, assets, watermark, footer or
  margins. Background graphics must remain ON for CSS-embedded assets to print.
- Oversized files can silently prevent the native download control from appearing
  on the recipient's client. A leaner file restores reliable delivery.

TRANSPORT COPY — OPTIONAL:
- Where a still-smaller copy helps transport, a near-lossless copy may be produced
  by quantizing only the flat brand raster assets (watermark, logos, seal,
  signature) to a reduced palette. Keep the full-fidelity file as the
  authoritative deliverable and label the reduced file clearly as a web/transport
  copy. Never quantize away legibility or brand fidelity on the authoritative file.

DELIVERY CHANNELS, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE:
1. Native self-contained HTML download control for the on-disk file.
2. Plain, resolvable file links (for example, the user's OneDrive) presented as
   plain text. Plain links render even when a recipient's client is intermittently
   blocking cards, buttons or download chips.
3. A simple link hub only when its links point to fully resolvable absolute URLs.

DELIVERY RULES:
- Prefer plain-text links as the resilient fallback whenever a recipient reports
  that buttons, cards or download chips are not rendering.
- Do not attempt to move binary or image-bearing files through chat text; binary
  content cannot be reproduced faithfully in a message. Route such files through a
  file channel (download control or file storage), never through transcription.
- Confirm with the recipient that the delivered link or control actually opened
  before treating the task as delivered.

======================================================================
28B. CHANNEL-FAILURE FALLBACK -- INLINE VERIFICATION RENDER
======================================================================
Section 28A governs delivery when the RECIPIENT'S CLIENT struggles to render a
normally-sized delivery. This section governs the DIFFERENT condition where the
DELIVERY MECHANISM ITSELF is unavailable -- a file-upload tool, document-library
write, or direct file-send call errors, including on a trivial test file, such
that no file channel (native download, file-storage push, or link) can succeed
regardless of size or recipient client capability.

DISTINGUISHING THE TWO CONDITIONS:

- Recipient-rendering failure (Section 28A): the delivery call succeeds, but the
  recipient reports the file, button, card, or chip did not display or open.
- Channel failure (this section): the delivery call itself returns an error,
  including on a minimal probe file, indicating the transport layer -- not the
  recipient -- is the point of failure.

Confirm which condition applies with a minimal test before choosing a remedy:
if a trivial one-line file also fails to send or upload, treat it as a channel
failure and apply this section rather than retrying Section 28A's channel list
indefinitely.

INLINE VERIFICATION RENDER -- PROCEDURE:

1. Identify every large embedded binary payload in the deliverable (base64 image
   data URIs, embedded fonts, or other non-text blobs) that is not itself the
   subject of the current request.
2. Replace each such payload with a short, explicitly labeled placeholder string
   naming what was removed and stating it is byte-identical in the full-fidelity
   file (for example: "[TRIMMED FOR CHAT DELIVERY -- watermark image, byte-
   identical in the full package/file saved server-side]"). Never remove or
   alter surrounding structure, CSS rules, DOM, or text content -- only the
   binary payload itself is substituted.
3. Confirm the resulting file is materially smaller and consists entirely of
   plain text (HTML markup, CSS rules using var()-based tokens, JSON, or other
   inherently textual content) suitable for direct inline transmission.
4. Paste the complete resulting source inline in the chat response itself as
   the deliverable, exactly once, in full -- not truncated or summarized.
5. State plainly, in the same response, which specific elements were
   placeholder-substituted, and that the unmodified, full-fidelity original
   (with every real binary payload intact) remains saved and available through
   the normal file channel once it recovers.
6. This procedure does not alter, approximate, or lossily compress any text,
   markup, CSS, or structural content. Only non-text binary payloads unrelated
   to the current task are substituted, and only with explicit disclosure. It
   is a controlled, narrow exception to the Section 28A rule against moving
   binary content through chat text -- it never transcribes binary data itself,
   it substitutes a disclosed placeholder for it.

WHEN TO APPLY:

Apply this section proactively the moment any file-delivery tool call errors,
rather than waiting for the recipient to report a problem or retrying the same
failing channel repeatedly. Different chat interfaces and API-connected models
vary in file-upload size limits, binary-handling capability, and whether file
delivery is supported at all -- this section is the universal fallback that
functions inside any text-capable interface regardless of that variance.

RECOVERY:

Once the normal file channel is confirmed working again (for example, a later
trivial probe file succeeds), resume standard Section 28A delivery for the
full-fidelity file and note the successful handoff. The inline verification
render is a stopgap for continuity and review, not a permanent replacement for
the authoritative full-fidelity deliverable.

FAILURE CONDITIONS SPECIFIC TO THIS SECTION:

- Treating a channel failure as if it were a recipient-rendering problem, and
  retrying Section 28A's channel list indefinitely without ever falling back.
- Silently altering text, markup, CSS values, or structure while trimming --
  only binary payloads may be substituted, and only with disclosure.
- Failing to disclose which elements were placeholder-substituted.
- Failing to note that the full-fidelity original remains available once the
  channel recovers.
- Attempting to transcribe actual binary data into chat text instead of using
  a disclosed placeholder.

28C. ASSET HYDRATION AND ASSEMBLY (GOVERNED BY KERNEL MODULE 03 / 05 / 10)
======================================================================
The stored quotation payload is the TOKENIZED template. Every binary brand asset
is held exactly once in brand_assets and referenced from the template by an
opaque placeholder of the form {{GSSC_ASSET:name}}.

WHY THIS EXISTS:
Section 28A already requires single-embed Base64 asset deduplication. Storing an
asset both in the asset repository and again inside the template violated that
rule and inflated the shipped package, because template bytes are Base64-encoded
a second time on the way into the container. Tokenizing removes the duplication
without altering one character of text, markup, geometry or typography.

HYDRATION IS MANDATORY BEFORE DELIVERY:
The tokenized template is a STORAGE form, not a deliverable. It must never be
sent to a client, opened as a finished document, or treated as the rendered
quotation. Hydrate first.

PROCEDURE (executable form: python gssc_runtime.py hydrate <package> -o out.html):
1. Decode quotation_template_payload_base64 to UTF-8 text.
2. For each token {{GSSC_ASSET:name}}, look up brand_assets[name].
3. Replace the token with: data:<mime>;base64,<base64>
   using the entry's own mime and base64 values, verbatim.
4. Replace tokens ONLY. Never edit surrounding markup during hydration.
5. Verify each decoded asset against its sha256_of_decoded_image before use.
6. The hydrated result must equal assembly.verification.hydrated_template_sha256.
   If it does not, stop: the package is damaged or has been altered. Do not
   deliver, and do not attempt a partial repair.

FAILURE CONDITIONS:
- An unresolved token remains in a client-facing file. HARD STOP.
- An asset hash does not match its declared value. HARD STOP.
- A brand_assets entry is orphaned (declared but never referenced). Report it;
  it indicates the template and the asset repository have diverged.
- The hydrated hash does not match the declared verification value. HARD STOP.

STANDALONE RENDERING:
A hydrated file is fully self-contained and renders offline with no external
request, exactly as before. This preserves the single-file offline portability
principle. The saving is in transport and storage, never in the delivered
artifact.

======================================================================
23C. FOOTER AND GEOMETRIC OVERLAP -- CUMULATIVE CURSOR (GOVERNED BY KERNEL MODULE 10 / 17)
======================================================================
HONESTY NOTE: this shares Section 23A's calibrated approximation and none of
its certainty. It is not a rendered screenshot. What changes is not the
accuracy of the estimate but its RESOLUTION: 23A answers whether a page is too
full on aggregate; it cannot answer which block crosses the footer, or by how
many pixels. Those are the two facts an operator needs before applying the
Section 23 escalation ladder, and neither was obtainable before this section.

METHOD:

Walk the FLOWED body blocks of each page in document order. Maintain a running
Y cursor beginning at margin-top plus that page's own body padding-top. After
each block, test its own bottom edge against two boundaries, both derived from
geometry already declared in Module 10, not invented here:

  SOFT  page-height - margin-bottom - body padding-bottom. The block has
        entered the page's own reserve. Still inside the margin, but the
        buffer is gone.
  HARD  page-height - margin-bottom. The block has entered the footer band
        itself -- running footer, seal, folio and contact anchor.

On the universal master these resolve to a hard line at 1003px (1123 - 120) and
a soft line at 977px or 981px depending on the page's own bottom padding.

Absolutely-positioned locked chrome -- masthead, colophon, margin rail,
watermark -- is EXCLUDED from the cursor. It does not participate in flow, and
including it causes the walk to mis-attribute an overflow to a footer element
that never flowed. The first prototype of this section did exactly that,
naming .footer-secondary as the offending block on a forced fixture whose real
cause was an injected paragraph several elements earlier.

Figure heights, table cell type sizes and the declared block separation share
the SAME cursor rather than being measured separately, so the walk is not a
prose-only estimate.

VALIDATION ON RECORD (21 September 2026): executed against the real hydrated 2.10.0
derivative and against a deliberately forced-overflow fixture. Real derivative:
5 pages, all PASS, smallest headroom 215px on page 5.
Forced fixture: correctly FAILED, naming the offending block and its overflow
in pixels. Both branches confirmed to compute from real arithmetic, not a
default.

SCOPE LIMIT:

Raster image heights, CSS rendering defects and webfont-loading failure remain
outside this check, as they remain outside every other check in this package.
The header-boundary and marginalia-boundary variants of the same cursor are a
direct extension of this method and are NOT yet built.
